prompt.context: Euro Logistics is a big logistics company. It wants to improve its customer satisfaction index.
prompt.question: What should they do?

clarifying_info.q: What kind of logistics company is Euro Logistics?
clarifying_info.a: It is a large logistics company similar to Maersk. They provide logistics services only in Europe and have many trucks, sea port terminals all around Europe, and cargo ships.

clarifying_info.q: Why is the company focused on customer satisfaction?
clarifying_info.a: The logistics market is very competitive and Euro Logistics understands that offering better customer service is a good way to differentiate themselves in this market.

exhibits.title: Customer Satisfaction Survey
exhibits.shows: A survey filled by over 250 companies showing customer satisfaction scores (0-100) for different service dimensions, ranked by importance, across 8 European countries: Germany, England, Norway, Sweden, Italy, Netherlands, Ireland, and Scotland/France. Scores above 75 are considered good.

framework: Map the customer value chain end-to-end: order placement, order tracking, delivery, billing, and post-delivery customer service
Assess current performance on each dimension by country/segment
Identify gaps versus the 75-point threshold for each dimension
Prioritize improvement initiatives by impact (breadth of countries affected, score gap) and feasibility
Estimate investment required and financial return (payback period)
Design implementation roadmap for priority systems/processes

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 1. What can you conclude from this table? Is there a particular measure or country that Euro Logistics should pay special attention to?
questions.guidance: Strong answer identifies: (1) Billing scores are below 75 in nearly every country and Billing is ranked as most important by the most countries — it is the top priority. (2) Order Tracking scores are also consistently below 75 and ranked as most important in several countries (Norway, Italy, Ireland, Scotland/France). (3) Customer Service scores are generally high (above 75 in most countries) — a relative strength. (4) Delivery Time has mixed scores; the interviewer will clarify that delays are caused by customs, so Euro Logistics can only improve by setting more realistic delivery deadlines rather than fixing internal operations. Candidate should recommend focusing on Billing and Order Tracking systems first.

questions.prompt: Euro Logistics wants to improve its Billing and Order Tracking systems. Our team estimates it will cost 5 M Euros to buy each of these new systems, but we estimate the new systems will reduce the churn rate (% of customers lost per year) by 20%. Should they do it? What is the payback period of this investment?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask for current revenues, current churn rate, and net margin. The investment payback is under 2 years so the recommendation is to invest. Key insight: the savings figure is the revenue no longer lost due to reduced churn, not directly the net margin — though the problem is structured so that revenues lost = the relevant flow to offset the investment.

math.setup: Total investment = 5 M + 5 M = 10 M euros. Revenue currently lost per year due to churn = Current Yearly Revenues x Churn Rate. Savings from new systems = Revenue lost per year x Churn Reduction. Payback Period = Total Investment / Annual Savings.
steps: Current Yearly Revenues = 150 M euros (given upon request)
Revenues lost per year = 150 M x 25% = 37.5 M euros
Savings provided by new systems = 37.5 M x 20% = 7.5 M euros
Payback period = 10 M / 7.5 M = 1.33 years = approximately 1 year and 4 months
math.answer: Payback period is approximately 1 year and 4 months, which is less than the 2-year goal. Euro Logistics should invest in both systems.

recommendation: Euro Logistics should invest in upgrading both the Billing and Order Tracking systems at a combined cost of 10 M euros.
The investment pays back in approximately 1 year and 4 months, well within the 2-year target, by reducing annual churn-driven revenue loss from 37.5 M to 30 M euros (saving 7.5 M per year).
For Delivery Time, Euro Logistics cannot control customs delays but should set more realistic delivery deadlines to improve customer perception.
Customer Service scores are already strong and do not require immediate investment.
risks: Churn reduction of 20% is an estimate; actual reduction may be lower if customers switch for reasons beyond Billing and Tracking.
Systems integration may take time, delaying the payback.
Other competitors may simultaneously improve their systems, eroding the differentiation benefit.
next_steps: Conduct vendor selection for Billing and Order Tracking system upgrades.
Define realistic delivery timelines in consultation with customs authorities by country.
Set up KPIs to track score improvements post-implementation and rerun the customer satisfaction survey at 6-month intervals.
